items.q: Which of the following will cause spare capacity in a business to RISE?
opts: New competitors are entering the market.
The business closes some factories.
The business's product becomes more fashionable.
There is a successful advertising campaign.
items.why: New competitors entering the market will take customers away, reducing demand for this business's products. With lower demand but the same capacity, spare capacity increases. B reduces capacity itself. C and D increase demand. Spare capacity = capacity minus output. It rises when demand falls (keeping capacity the same) or when capacity increases (keeping demand the same).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Decreasing government subsidies on agriculture would be:
opts: Fiscal policy encouraging more open trade
Fiscal policy increasing protectionism
Monetary policy encouraging more open trade
Monetary policy increasing protectionism
items.why: Subsidies are fiscal policy (government spending/tax). Reducing subsidies removes protection from domestic producers, exposing them to international competition = encouraging more open trade. Subsidies = fiscal policy. Interest rates = monetary policy.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which of the following is the best example of a business decision relating to the 'Process' element of the 7Ps?
opts: A bank redecorating its branch interiors with modern furniture and digital screens to create a more welcoming and professional physical environment for customers.
A bank introducing a mobile app that lets customers open accounts in under five minutes.
A bank recruiting and training multilingual staff to serve a diverse local community more effectively and improve customer satisfaction.
A bank sponsoring a local charity event and running a targeted social media campaign to raise brand awareness among younger demographics.
items.why: Process refers to the systems, procedures and flow of activities through which a service is delivered to the customer. A streamlined account-opening app is a process improvement. Redecorating is Physical evidence; multilingual staff is People; charity sponsorship is Promotion.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Demographic segmentation divides a market by variables such as age, gender and income.
Statement 2: Psychographic segmentation divides a market by variables such as region and postcode.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Demographic segmentation uses measurable personal characteristics such as age, gender and income — this is correct. Psychographic segmentation uses lifestyle, values and attitudes; dividing by region or postcode is geographic segmentation. Students often confuse psychographic with geographic.
items.label: New question

items.q: A food manufacturer buys a direct competitor AND a food wholesaler. This is:
opts: Backward vertical and forward vertical integration
Conglomerate integration
Horizontal and backward vertical integration
Horizontal and forward vertical integration
items.why: Buying a direct competitor = horizontal integration (same stage of production). Buying a food wholesaler = forward vertical integration (moving towards the customer/distribution stage). A manufacturer selling to a wholesaler is moving forward in the supply chain. The manufacturer is at production stage. A wholesaler is closer to the customer (forward).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Competitive pricing means a business sets its price based on the prices charged by its rivals.
Statement 2: Price skimming is most suitable when a product is entering a highly competitive market with low barriers to entry.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Competitive pricing is correctly defined as setting prices in line with or relative to competitors. Price skimming works best when the product is innovative or unique and faces little direct competition; high barriers to entry allow the business to charge a premium before rivals enter. In a highly competitive, low-barrier market, skimming would cause customers to switch immediately.
items.label: New question

items.q: Prestige Auto Group sells four product lines. 'ClassicDrive' has a low market share in a high-growth market. 'TurboMax' has a high market share in a high-growth market. According to the Boston Matrix, which labels correctly describe ClassicDrive and TurboMax respectively?
opts: Star; Cash cow
Dog; Star
Problem child; Star
Problem child; Cash cow
items.why: In the Boston Matrix, a product with low market share in a high-growth market is a Problem child (also called Question mark). A product with high market share in a high-growth market is a Star. TurboMax becomes a Cash cow only when market growth slows, so Cash cow is incorrect here.
items.label: New question

items.q: One high street bank merges with another high street bank. This is:
opts: Backward vertical integration
Diversification
Forward vertical integration
Horizontal integration
items.why: Two businesses at the same stage of the same industry merging = horizontal integration. Both are high street banks (identical business type). Same industry, same stage of production = horizontal.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Meadow Care is a private care home business. It trains all staff to greet residents by name and to use a consistent, calm communication style. Which element of the extended marketing mix (7Ps) does this practice most directly relate to?
opts: Process
Physical evidence
People
Promotion
items.why: The 'People' element of the 7Ps relates to the employees who deliver the service and how their behaviour, appearance and attitude affect the customer experience. Training staff in consistent, personalised behaviour is a direct People decision. 'Process' refers to the systems and procedures by which the service is delivered, which is a common distractor here.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using a long-term bank loan rather than issuing new share capital to finance expansion?
opts: New share capital dilutes the ownership and control of existing shareholders
Interest on the loan must be paid regardless of the business's profitability
Loan finance is only available to publicly listed companies
Using a bank loan reduces the business's credit rating automatically
items.why: A key disadvantage of debt finance is that interest payments are legally obligatory even if the business makes a loss, increasing financial risk. Option A is actually a disadvantage of share capital, not loans. Option C is incorrect — private companies can also borrow from banks. Option D is not an automatic or inevitable consequence.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business replaces workers with machinery. 10% increase in capacity/output, 5% increase in unit costs. This is an example of:
opts: More capital intensive and economies of scale
More capital intensive and diseconomies of scale
More labour intensive and economies of scale
More labour intensive and diseconomies of scale
items.why: Replacing workers with machinery = more capital intensive. Unit costs increased by 5%, which means the business is experiencing diseconomies of scale (costs rising as scale increases). Unit costs went UP despite increased output. Rising unit costs = diseconomies.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A market map helps a business identify gaps in the market that may represent opportunities for new products.
Statement 2: A market map plots competitors along two chosen axes and always uses price and quality as those axes.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: A market map does help identify gaps where customer needs may be unmet — Statement 1 is correct. However, while price and quality are common axes, a business can choose any two relevant variables (e.g. age appeal and exclusivity), so Statement 2 is false. Students often assume price and quality are the only valid axes.
items.label: New question

items.q: The 7 'P's of the marketing mix include:
opts: Process
Positioning
Productivity
Primary market research
items.why: Process is one of the 7Ps. The others listed are not part of the 7Ps. The 7Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion, People, Process, Physical Evidence.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Hartley's Honey produces specialist raw Manuka honey sold only through independent health food retailers at a premium price. Which of the following best describes a disadvantage of operating in a niche market for Hartley's Honey?
opts: The business will face intense competition from large, well-resourced rivals who can undercut its premium pricing through economies of scale.
The small customer base makes the business vulnerable if consumer tastes change.
It will be unable to charge premium prices because the limited number of independent retailers gives consumers a wider range of comparable alternatives.
Niche markets require heavy investment in targeted digital and print advertising in order to reach a sufficiently large segment of specialist consumers.
items.why: A key disadvantage of a niche market is that the limited customer base means any shift in consumer preferences or a new competitor can have a disproportionate impact on sales. Option A is more characteristic of mass markets; premium pricing (C) is typically an advantage of niche positioning; niche businesses generally avoid mass-market advertising (D).
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Speed of response is an operational objective that is always in conflict with quality.

Statement 2: Dependability (reliability of delivery) can itself be a source of competitive advantage for a business.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: speed and quality can be complementary — well-designed processes (such as lean systems) can deliver quickly and to high quality simultaneously. Statement 2 is true: consistently meeting promised delivery dates builds customer trust and loyalty, differentiating the business from less reliable rivals.
items.label: New question

items.q: Market capitalisation is the total value of a company's:
opts: Assets
Dividends paid to shareholders
Shares, based on the current share price
Shares, based on the original share price
items.why: Market capitalisation = total number of shares x current share price. It represents the total market value of all outstanding shares. Market cap uses the current price, not the original issue price.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: In which situation is a business most likely to use outsourcing? A: High utilisation, High predictability B: High utilisation, Low predictability C: Low utilisation, High predictability D: Low utilisation, Low predictability
opts: Situation A
Situation B
Situation C
Situation D
items.why: High capacity utilisation means the business is already near full capacity, and low predictability of demand means demand can spike unexpectedly. Outsourcing provides flexible extra capacity to handle unpredictable demand surges without investing in permanent capacity. Outsourcing makes most sense when you're already stretched (high utilisation) and can't predict when you'll need extra capacity (low predictability).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Novo Tech launches a new smart home device into a competitive market where several similar products already exist. The marketing director recommends setting a low launch price to build market share quickly. Which pricing strategy is the marketing director recommending?
opts: Price skimming
Penetration pricing
Psychological pricing
Cost-plus pricing
items.why: Penetration pricing involves setting a deliberately low price at launch to attract customers and gain market share rapidly, which fits the scenario. Price skimming is the opposite — a high initial price to maximise revenue from early adopters, typically used when a product is unique. Students often confuse the two launch strategies.
items.label: New question

items.q: A farmer takes over a retailer to sell its produce. This is:
opts: Horizontal integration
Backward vertical integration
Forward vertical integration
Conglomerate integration
items.why: A farmer (producer) buying a retailer (closer to customer) = forward vertical integration. The farmer is moving down the supply chain towards the end consumer. Producer -> Retailer = forward (towards customer). If the retailer bought the farm, that would be backward.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: According to Porter's Five Forces, which event HELPS a business's profitability?
opts: A decrease in supplier power
A new entrant into the market
An increase in buyer power
New product development by a competitor
items.why: Lower supplier power means the business can negotiate better prices/terms, reducing costs and improving profitability. B, C, and D all increase competitive pressure and threaten profitability. Porter's Five Forces: any force that weakens improves your profitability. Lower supplier power = you have more bargaining strength.
items.label: Past paper question
